critiques.summary:
Round 2 resolved both of my blocking concerns from round 1, and no remaining gap can plausibly reorder the ranking.

(1) Rejection-by-absence on H2 is closed with positive evidence: exchange-gateway — the market-data-service consumer on the protobuf path — was actually queried and is flat across both the 11:56Z deploy and the 12:04Z onset (latency_p99 121-139ms, 5xx 0.11-0.32%, upstream_error_rate ~0.3% constant, request_rate/cpu flat) and logged zero WARN+ and zero 'proto' lines (F19-F23). That is direct evidence, not inference from a truncated pull.

(2) The persistence check was run: CPU pinned 98.6-99.5%, p99 ~2540-2745ms, error_rate ~12-13%, GreeksV2 WARNs to 13:58:44Z, deadline ERRORs to 13:58:55Z, and no revert line exists — the only greeks_v2 log line in the window is the 12:04:16Z apply at rollout_pct=100 (F25-F30, F29). A transient deploy effect (H2) or a self-limited one-off saturation (H3) would have decayed; this did not.

On the still-unverified load-bearing link, the critic's round-1 request was answered honestly and negatively: no per-request calculator-path metric or log exists (F31-F33, F36), so the "5%->100% share" can never be measured with this telemetry. Crucially, this is a permanent observability limit, not evidence in H3's favour. The decisive discrimination was therefore run by the other available route, and it favors H1: the ONLY candidate trigger anywhere in the fleet in the window is cfg-3120 at 12:04:00Z (F3, F4 — retry returned partial:false, so the set is complete), it lands on the exact minute of a sharp multi-signal step (p99 57.5ms@12:02 -> 1297.7ms@12:04; CPU 40%->99%; error_rate 0.24%->8.52% in the 12:05 bucket; first GreeksV2 WARN 12:05:21Z, absent before 12:04:30 — F9, F10, F14, F35, F37), the mechanism is named in pricing-engine's own logs (compute-bound 'GreeksV2Calculator: Monte-Carlo paths=20000' blowing the internal 2000ms budget, calculator=GreeksV2 deadline errors — F12, F17), volume and memory are flat so it is neither load- nor GC-driven (F10, F11, F30, F24), and order-service latency tracks pricing-engine plus baseline hop overhead (F15) with errors naming a pricing-engine downstream call (F8). H3 is H1's mechanism with no driver, and the one change-free driver it posits (work-mix/request-composition shift) is contradicted by flat pricing-engine and market-data-service request_rate across onset (F11, F24, F30). H2 is refuted on timing (8-minute silent gap, no metric step anywhere) and mechanism (compute path, not parse path). H4 is refuted by flat redis-cache CPU and the internal-compute localisation (F16, F17).

Residual issues are secondary, not blocking: F9 carries an UNVERIFIED tag despite the same series being independently described by a VERIFIED query (F14), and per-2-min WARN/ERROR tallies are approximate due to truncation (truncated:true) though the steady non-decaying trend is reliable. I set the cap at 0.8 rather than the stated 0.72+ headroom to reflect the unmeasurable flag-effect link.

challenges.issue: The single load-bearing link — that the greeks_v2 ramp actually shifted ~95% of quote traffic onto GreeksV2 at 12:04 — remains unverified and is now shown to be UNMEASURABLE with this telemetry (no per-flag/per-calculator metric, no per-request calculator log, no legacy log series; F31-F33, F36). The causal chain therefore rests on a minute-level coincidence (cfg-3120 at 12:04:00Z with the 12:04-12:05 step) plus generic calculator logs. This is a real grounding weakness, but it is a permanent data-source limit rather than evidence favouring a competing origin, so it caps confidence rather than blocking the verdict.

F9 (the pricing-engine p99 step) is cited as support while carrying an UNVERIFIED tag. This is largely semantic — the same step is independently described by VERIFIED findings F14 and F15 — but the chain should not lean on the UNVERIFIED node.

H3 was kept alive at 0.08 only because the flag-effect link is unmeasured, not because any positive evidence supports change-free saturation. That residual probability is properly represented by a lower confidence cap rather than by further tool spend.

The rejection relies on zero effect at exchange-gateway and market-data-service, but exchange-gateway's own upstream_latency_ms series to market-data-service was never retrieved (budget_exhausted). Its end-to-end p99, 5xx, upstream_error_rate, request_rate and cpu are all flat, so this omits only a confirmation, not a discriminator.
